sentences.text: Appearance:
Shri L.N.Soni, learned senior advocate with Ms. Prach  advocate for the applicant  Shri K.K.Tiwari, learned GA for the State.
ORDER Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is first bail application filed under section 439 of the Cr.P.C. / 483 of the BNSS, 2023 for grant of bail to the applicant, in connection with FIR/Crime No.134/2024 Date:-(Not mentioned)
registered at P.S.-M.G. Road, District- Indore (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 474, 120-B and 34 of the IPC.

2. Prosecution story, in brief is that at the relevant time the co-accused Mohammad Sajid was proprietor of Neu Construction company, co-accused Abhay Singh Rathore was posted as Executive Engineer, drainage department of Indore Municipal Corporation (hereinafter referred to as IMC).

Co-accused persons Samar Singh Parmar and Anil Kumar Garg were NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:6674 2 MCRC-5821-2025 posted as Deputy Director and co-accused Rameshwar Parmar was Assistant Auditor in Audit Department of IMC.
Co-accused Imran Khan is proprietor of Crystal Enterprises, co-accused Mousam Vyas is proprietor of Ishwar Enterprises.
Co-accused Rahul Badera and present applicant Mohammad Zakir are proprietor of Jhanvi Enterprises and King Enterprises and are also contractor.
Co-accused persons Uday Singh @ Ankush Bhadoriya, Chetan Bhadoriya, Raj Kumar and Murli Dharan were also posted in Accounts Department of IMC.

During 11.12.2020 - 03.05.2024, present applicant and co-accused persons conspired to gain wrongfully by Mohd Jakir vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93343256/
1 carrying out embezzlement of the funds of IMC and they forged the work order, measurement books, work completion certificate, bills etc. and on the basis of forged documents, they had withdrawn a sum of Rs.7.5 Crores from the funds of IMC.

sentences.text: As alleged applicant received amount of Rs.1,06,00,000/- in his bank account.
Co-accused persons Samar Singh Parmar, Anil Kumar Garg and Rameshwar Parmar have audited fake bills and they have approved the aforesaid bills for payment.
Bills were passed for payment after the date mentioned in the note-sheet by the accused firms.
But no objection was raised by the co-accused persons/ officers posted in the audit department of IMC.
Thereby the accused persons forged documents and embezzled a huge amount of IMC.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant has not committed the offence and has falsely been implicated in the case.

It is submitted that co-accused persons Mohammad Siddique (order dated 7.2.2025 in MCRC No.53955/2024), Rajkumar Salvi (order dated 7.2.2025 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6674 3 MCRC-5821-2025 in MCRC No.54958/2024), Abhay Singh Rathore, (order dated 17.12.2024 in MCRC No.53260/2024), Mousan Vyas (order dated 17.12.2024 in MCRC No.54261/2024), Mohammad Imran (order dated 17.12.2024 in MCRC No.52460/2024), Rameshwar Parmar (order dated 9.12.2024 in MCRC No.46454/2024),
Aihetesham Khan (order dated 16.10.2024 in MCRC No.41857/2024) have been granted bail by the court.
He further submits that case of the present applicant is identical with the co-accused Siddique therefore he is also entitled for grant of bail.
It is also submitted that applicant is in custody since 28.04.2024.
After completion of investigation, charge sheet has been filed.
It is further submitted that applicant is ready to deposit the misappropriated amount i.e. 50% of Rs.1,06,00,000/-.
Conclusion of the trial will take sufficient long time for its disposal.

Under these circumstances,
prayer is made for grant of bail to the applicant.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the non-applicant/State has opposed the prayer of the applicant and prayed for its rejection.
However it is fairly submitted that case of the present applicant is identical with the co- accused Mohd. Siddique.

5. Having considered the submissions advanced from counsel for the parties, also considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the applicant is ready to deposit 50% of 1,06,00,000/- i.e.
Rs.53,00,000/-, without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
Hence, the application is allowed subject to depositing 50% of 1,06,00,000/- i.e. Rs.53,00,000/- before release from the jail.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6674 4 MCRC-5821-2025 6.

It is directed that the applicant- MOHD JAKIR be released on bail subject to depositing amount of Rs.53,00,000/-before the trial court and on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the trial Court during pendency of the trial.
It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of section 480 (3) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
